PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   B. Overload every socket
   C. Ignore burnt cables
   D. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun

2. When learning Ceramic Materials, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Ceramic Materials.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Ceramic Materials.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Ceramic Materials.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Ceramic Materials.

3. When learning Cutting Tools 15 4.2 Computer Software 6 5.0 Entrepreneurship 5.1 Bookkeeping 12, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Cutting Tools 15 4.2 Computer Software 6 5.0 Entrepreneurship 5.1 Bookkeeping 12.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Cutting Tools 15 4.2 Computer Software 6 5.0 Entrepreneurship 5.1 Bookkeeping 12.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Cutting Tools 15 4.2 Computer Software 6 5.0 Entrepreneurship 5.1 Bookkeeping 12.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Cutting Tools 15 4.2 Computer Software 6 5.0 Entrepreneurship 5.1 Bookkeeping 12.

4. When learning Visual Programming, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Visual Programming.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Visual Programming.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Visual Programming.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Visual Programming.

5. When learning Composite Materials 7 3.2 Ceramics 7 4.0 Tools and Production 4.1 Cutting Tools , the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Composite Materials 7 3.2 Ceramics 7 4.0 Tools and Production 4.1 Cutting Tools .
   B. Skip safety briefings for Composite Materials 7 3.2 Ceramics 7 4.0 Tools and Production 4.1 Cutting Tools .
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Composite Materials 7 3.2 Ceramics 7 4.0 Tools and Production 4.1 Cutting Tools .
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Composite Materials 7 3.2 Ceramics 7 4.0 Tools and Production 4.1 Cutting Tools .

6. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. International Cricket Team
   B. Input Cable Tester
   C. Information and Communication Technology
   D. Internal Cooking Timer

7. When learning Data Safety, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Data Safety.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Data Safety.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Safety.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Data Safety.

8. When learning Dimensioning, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Dimensioning.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Dimensioning.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Dimensioning.

9. When learning Composite Materials, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Composite Materials.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Composite Materials.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Composite Materials.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Composite Materials.

10. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Work alone with eyes closed
   B. Run with the tool
   C. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   D. Remove all guards

11. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Speaker
   B. Keyboard
   C. CPU
   D. Monitor

12. When learning Plain Scale Drawing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Plain Scale Drawing.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Plain Scale Drawing.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Plain Scale Drawing.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Plain Scale Drawing.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Plain Scale Drawing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
